accounts.prose: The merge engine folds newcomers left-to-right. Only plain objects are recursively combined; non-plain values—including arrays and class instances—replace the prior value. It copies own string and symbol properties, preserves enumerable versus nonenumerable status, skips `__proto__`, and leaves unmatched nested values by reference. `mergeAndCompare` applies a callback to every incoming own property after any recursive merge; despite README wording about values being “overwritten,” the implementation also invokes it when no prior value exists. `mergeAndConcat` supplies the extension callback, which concatenates only when both values are arrays and otherwise returns the newcomer.

referent.description: runtime deep-merge engine and its callback-based variants

qualifications: The callback-on-new-properties observation comes from implementation; the README describes the callback more narrowly as triggering when a value is overwritten.
Copying properties materializes their values and preserves enumerability, but does not preserve complete property descriptors.
The README explicitly cautions that retained nested references can link results to inputs.

accounts.prose: “Copies properties” here means all own string-named properties—including nonenumerable ones—and all own symbols are enumerated. Reading each property obtains its current value, so accessors are not preserved as accessors. The destination preserves only whether the property was enumerable: nonenumerable properties are recreated as writable and configurable data properties, while enumerable properties are installed by assignment. Thus complete descriptors such as getters, setters, read-only status, and nonconfigurability are not retained. The string key `__proto__` is skipped on both the retained-origin and incoming-property passes.

referent.description: property enumeration, descriptor handling, and prototype-poisoning guard in the merge implementation

qualifications: Property reads may invoke getters; that follows from the captured source’s indexed reads, but side effects were not tested.
The `__proto__` guard applies to that exact string key; symbols are not equal to it.
